title: DESIGN-LAB video ownership boundary (DL-P1-131 / DLDS-F080)
description: Machine-readable ownership boundary between DESIGN-LAB and a video host (Premiere Pro, Media Encoder, After Effects class of tool). Every entry names one operation, one owner and the rule that enforces the split. v2 replaces the free-text 'host_classes' field with 'host_capabilities': versioned capability-registry ids of the form 'capability:<domain>/<name>@<integer version>', mirroring the provider style ('provider:<domain>/<name>') frozen in provider-capability.schema.json. A rule that needs a host states 'host_capability_refs' as capability ids; the human-readable 'display_label' is display only and no logic may branch on it. A design-lab owner over rendered or encoded work is legal only with a measured host-live evidence reference, and the module additionally refuses a duplicate capability id, a reference the document does not declare, and a host- or shared-owned entry that declares no capability at all.

operations.description: The closed operation vocabulary. Each one must be declared exactly once by an entry.

host_capabilities.description: The capability-registry ids this boundary is allowed to reference. A rule referencing an id outside this list is refused by the module, which fails closed.

host_capability_refs.description: Versioned capability ids this operation depends on. May be empty only for an operation DESIGN-LAB owns outright; a host- or shared-owned entry must declare at least one (the module refuses an empty list there).

host_live_evidence_ref.description: Required when design-lab claims ownership of rendered or encoded work. A measured receipt identifier, not a path and not a URL.

capability_ref.description: Versioned capability-registry id, 'capability:<domain>/<name>@<integer version>' (for example 'capability:video/render@1'). The version is part of the identity: an unversioned id would silently re-point at a different capability. A free string or a product name is not a capability id.

display_label.description: Human-readable label for display only. It is prose, not a contract: no rule, validation or boundary decision may branch on it, and the module reads it in exactly one display accessor.
